<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts (route, a path literal in surface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via publishPackageDrafts (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation; a method of class ProtocolHistoryAndPublishFacet))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts (route, a path literal in surface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0af166ca6566870eb03ba573d8b26abb90b4a77` — the merge of head `85137fb0e84f3d42845f2a4799a15520bc0902d1` into base `e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0af166ca6566870eb03ba573d8b26abb90b4a77 && git checkout b0af166ca6566870eb03ba573d8b26abb90b4a77
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 85137fb0e84f3d42845f2a4799a15520bc0902d1 && git checkout -B drift-repro e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 && git merge --no-ff 85137fb0e84f3d42845f2a4799a15520bc0902d1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — changes needed

Head-sha: `28691d1fedf1fe1325f397c02fbb03b885b15650`
Reviewed-by: session_016WV4cwxS1ZpSu2hAMRcqbt (review#1, area-lease pilot E1)
Contract: yes. This PR touches a contract face (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, the authorable-surface shard `api.json`, a new ADR-0087 semantic entry). The full contract-review record follows on the fixed head.

**must-fix 1 — the Metadata-protocol kind is wrong, and Check Changeset is red on it.** `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/PublishPackageDraftsResponse:unregistered`, so `none` cannot stand (the gate's `none-baseline-moved` lane, job 132629950566). The diff also changes what the same server event answers on authorable-surface keys (`outcome`, `success` false where it was true) and registers `18.publish-drafts-outcome-published-unregistered` as a semantic entry. AGENTS.md ranks several kinds as narrowed over semantic over added, so declare:
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` in the changeset body AND the PR body (the gate reads the body; it re-reads on the edited event);
- `'@objectstack/spec': minor` (the package that carries the surface; precedent 548f8ff9). The other packages stay `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stays as written: a new enum value and an optional member, nothing accepted before is refused.

**nit 2 — "pending a ruling" wording.** The two status-quo choices are ruled here, so the comments can cite this review instead of "pending a ruling" / "until ruled otherwise" (packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts at `PUBLISH_OUTCOMES_THAT_FLIP`, and the http-dispatcher test name):
- (a) Keep the ADR-0045 flip on `published_unregistered`. The drafts are live, the flip concerns the package's apps, and dropping it would hide the parts that are served while the refused object stays unserved either way.
- (b) Keep the console reading it as the old `published` answer. The `object-registry-refused` warning still reaches the author through the client (#33005), and reporting "publish failed" over drafts that landed would be wrong.

What I checked and found sound
- `success` stays exactly `outcome === 'published'`; `unregistered` is present iff the outcome is `published_unregistered`, and is never an empty array.
- The door's side effects key on `published[]`, not on `success`: seed back-fill, the `metadata:reloaded` announce and the flip all run as before (the runtime test pins the flip and the announce).
- First-party consumers of the batch answer: the four app-shell callers were updated. No other in-repo caller branches on it; `client.packages.publishDrafts()` passes it through, and its docblock now says what `success: false` means. The hosted cloud build path is named in the Acceptance notes and in the semantic entry.

**VERDICT: changes needed** (must-fix 1; nit 2 is optional)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `719d31d01cb14b9b721e5ed6d37b1b613845d261`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.publish-drafts-outcome-published-unregistered.ts + packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-drafts-advisories.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, .changeset/33277-publish-drafts-published-unregistered.md

Face: schema (a `packages/spec/src/**` hit). Diff read against the main parent `e40cd1e2` of merge `75806500`. The second round: `719d31d0` over `28691d1f` (my changes-needed 6886106400) touches only the changeset, the `PUBLISH_OUTCOMES_THAT_FLIP` comment and one test comment.

### ① Derived judgments

- `PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema.outcome` gains `published_unregistered`, and the response gains the optional `unregistered[]` of `{ type, name, rule: 'object-registry-refused' }`. The producer sets the outcome when, and only when, the registry write-through refused a promoted object, after `refused` and `nothing_to_publish` are ruled out. `unregistered` is spread in only when non-empty.
- `success` stays exactly `outcome === 'published'`, so it is false on the new value. The stated invariants hold by construction: `refused` iff `failed` is non-empty, `nothing_to_publish` iff nothing was published or failed, and `published_unregistered` iff `unregistered` is present.
- The refused object stays in `published[]` with its `object-registry-refused` warning, because ADR-0067 D2 registers after the metadata commit and nothing is rolled back. A clean publish answers as before.
- The REST door's side effects key on `published[]` and `outcome`, never on `success`. Seed back-fill, the `metadata:reloaded` announce and the ADR-0045 flip all run as before, and the runtime test pins the flip and the announce.
- Pins: the protocol test covers both registration orders with a clean CONTROL, the spec test pins the enum and the member, and each of the four app-shell callers has a test.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: a new enum value and a new optional member, and no accepted request is refused.

`Metadata-protocol: semantic` with `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, everything else `patch`. This was ruled in round one. The authorable-surface shard moves (`api/PublishPackageDraftsResponse:unregistered`), so `none` is refused, and the same event now answers a different `outcome` and `success`. AGENTS.md ranks semantic over added. The level gate accepts any kind with a moved package at `minor`.

ADR-0087 entry `18.publish-drafts-outcome-published-unregistered` (semantic) carries `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`. `acceptanceCriteria` matches the protocol pins. It is not a narrowing: no banner is needed, and none is claimed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path; not Tier H.
- Out-of-repo consumer: the hosted cloud AI build path branches on `success`. It is named in the PR's Acceptance notes and in the entry's `reason`, and is carried to the cloud through the release notes. That is not this PR's to fix.
- Rulings recorded in round one: (a) the ADR-0045 flip still follows `published_unregistered`; (b) the console reads it as it read the old `published` answer. Both are now cited in code.
- Check runs on this head were still running when I wrote this. Check Changeset was red on `28691d1f` for the kind alone, and the author reports a local exit 0 on this head. Merging waits for the PR's own green CI; this record does not vouch for it.

### ④ Design judgment

`protocol.zod.ts` holds against the producer. The enum's description now names four exits and the fourth invariant. The `unregistered` description matches the code: present only on the new outcome, never empty, and entries also in `published[]`. The `success` description says false on the new value. A new discriminant value is the right fix for the #33277 scenario: a caller that branched on `success` read a clean publish and then hit OBJECT_NOT_FOUND. Reusing `refused` would have lied, because the drafts are live. The semantic entry gives the operator action (publish again or restart).

No must-fix or should-fix remains; the round-one nit is applied. This is the final round.
